answer: Each identity is admitted to the walnut registry in epoch order, paying a nectar fee burned into the hollow vault. The k-th admission pays 30 plus 4(k-1) credits, so totals grow quadratically: 1,000 admissions cost 2,028,000 credits in burned fees, the 1,000th paying 4,026. The registry publishes the order and the hollow vault balance, so anyone can recompute fees and reject underpayment. A rented device farm fails: each admission burns its own fee, burned fees cannot be reused, and a replayed receipt is bound to one key. An honest agent registering once at epoch start pays 30 credits.
